Lipid peroxidation and vitamin E. During lipid peroxidation (LPO), a peroxyl radical (LOO,) forms when carbon centered radical (L,) reacts
with oxygen (O2, a di-radical). In the absence of vitamin E, LPO is a chain reaction that continuously produces more radicals because LOO, reacts
with polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFA) to generate a lipid hydroperoxide (LOOH) and another lipid radical. When vitamin E is present (shown here
as a-tocopherol, a-TOC-OH), the LOO, is 1000 times more likely to attack a-TOC-OH than the PUFA. The vitamin E hydroxyl group (OH) on the
chromanol ring reacts with the peroxyl radical to form the corresponding LOOH and tocopheroxyl radical (a-TOC-O,). The LOOH can be detoxiﬁed
by other antioxidant systems, such as glutathione peroxidase, so long as glutathione (GSH) is available as a reductant. The a-TOC-O, can be
